title: Environment configuration
description: Framework-neutral TypeScript schema for environment variables that validates a caller-supplied record at startup, returns a frozen typed object, reports every problem by key without echoing values, redacts secrets, and renders .env.example text.

notes: Requires a TypeScript 5.0+ build (const type parameters infer string choices); no runtime packages.
The module never reads process.env, Deno.env, files, or globals; the caller passes a record such as process.env, Deno.env.toObject(), a Cloudflare Workers env, or import.meta.env.
Primarily for server/startup code. It can run in a browser bundle, but anything bundled to a client is public regardless of the secret() marker.
Tested on Node.js 22 in this repository; other runtimes are expected to work because only ES2022 built-ins and URL are used, but were not executed here.

configuration: Declare a schema with str/num/bool/url/list/json/secret fields; chain .optional(), .secret(), .describe(text), and .example(text) as needed.
Call defineConfig(schema).parse(source) once at startup with the runtime's environment record and let ConfigError stop the process; use safeParse for a result object instead.
Use toExample() to generate or check a committed .env.example, and redact(config) or JSON.stringify(config) for safe startup logging.
limitations: Does not load .env files, expand ${VAR} references, watch for changes, or fetch from secret managers.
Empty strings are treated as missing. Defaults are trusted schema values and are not re-validated against min/max/pattern rules.
secret() controls rendering by this module only; it does not encrypt values or stop application code from logging config.KEY directly.
json() values are not deep-frozen, and a json validate function's own error text is replaced by a fixed message.
Only own properties of the source record are read; proxy or getter-based environment objects must expose schema keys as own properties.
